source.author: ov
source.text: Clamanti cutis est summos direpta per artus, nec quicquam nisi vulnus erat; cruor undique manat, detectique patent nervi, trepidaeque sine ulla pelle micant venae; salientia viscera posses et perlucentes numerare in pectore fibras.
source.text_original: Clamanti cutis est summos direpta per artus, / nec quicquam nisi vulnus erat; cruor undique manat, / detectique patent nervi, trepidaeque sine ulla / pelle micant venae; salientia viscera posses / et perlucentes numerare in pectore fibras.
source.text_english: As he cried out, his skin was ripped away from all his limbs, and he was nothing but a wound; blood flows everywhere, and the exposed sinews lie open, and the trembling veins quiver with no skin at all; you could count the beating entrails and the translucent fibers in his chest.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Protulit ut crinem densis luctatus in extis ignis et escendit salientia viscera tauri, ecce sacer totusque dei per litora Mopsus immanis visu vittamque comamque per auras surgentem laurusque rotat.
reuse.text_original: Protulit ut crinem densis luctatus in extis / ignis et escendit salientia viscera tauri, / ecce sacer totusque dei per litora Mopsus / immanis visu vittamque comamque per auras / surgentem laurusque rotat.
reuse.text_english: As the fire, struggling amid the crowded entrails, brought forth the hair and climbed over the quivering innards of the bull, behold, the sacred Mopsus, wholly possessed by the god, terrible to see, was moving along the shore, his fillet and hair rising through the air, and he was brandishing laurel branches.
